steps.tx: Ameloblastoma, benign yet locally aggressive odontogenic tumour of posterior mandible, expands multilocular soap bubble radiolucencies, resorbing roots and cortex while rarely metastasising. Its paradox is local fury without spread: **ameloblastoma, benign but locally aggressive jaw tumour**. Posterior mandible around the third molar is the classic site, often found incidentally on panoramic films.
steps.say: Soap bubble mandible expansion in a young adult is ameloblastoma; benign histology, aggressive geography.

vis.caption: Ameloblastoma with multilocular mandibular expansion and follicular histology.

steps.tx: Follicular and plexiform patterns of ameloblastic epithelium with peripheral columnar palisading and central stellate reticulum like cells recur across variants, unicystic forms behaving kinder when truly unicystic mural invasion excluded. Pattern literacy is **ameloblastoma histological variants and behaviour**. Desmoplastic variants blend into dense collagen and favour the anterior maxilla, unlike conventional posterior tumours.
steps.say: Peripheral palisading around stellate centres names ameloblastoma; unicystic type earns gentler surgery only when mural invasion is excluded.

left.title: Unicystic ameloblastoma
points: Conservative surgery if no mural invasion

steps.tx: Curettage of solid ameloblastoma leaves microscopic medullary extensions that recur in most patients, so resection with one to one and a half centimetre margins and reconstruction is definitive. Margin discipline defines **ameloblastoma resection over curettage**. Recurrence after curettage can exceed fifty percent, compared with far lower rates after segmental resection.
steps.say: Curetted ameloblastoma returns; resect it with margins the first time and reconstruct the jaw.

steps.tx: Odontogenic keratocyst, now keratocystic odontogenic tumour in many classifications, lines jaws with thin parakeratinised corrugated epithelium, daughter cysts, and high recurrence from fragile lining remnants. Its recurrence engine is the **odontogenic keratocyst (OKC)**. A corrugated parakeratin surface over palisaded basal cells separates keratocyst lining from dentigerous cyst lining.
steps.say: Thin corrugated lining, daughter cysts, stubborn recurrence: odontogenic keratocyst punishes incomplete removal.

vis.caption: Jaw and oral anatomy framing odontogenic cysts and tumours.

steps.tx: Multiple odontogenic keratocysts in a young patient demand Gorlin syndrome evaluation: basal cell carcinomas, palmar pits, bifid ribs, falx calcification, and PTCH1 mutation counselling. That syndromic trigger is **Gorlin syndrome (naevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome)**. Calcified falx cerebri on skull film offers a cheap clue when jaw cysts suggest the syndrome.
steps.say: Multiple jaw keratocysts in youth mean Gorlin syndrome; count skin cancers, pits, and ribs next.

steps.tx: Dentigerous cysts around unerupted crowns and radicular cysts at dead tooth apices complete the odontogenic cyst triage, separated radiographically by relation to crown, apex, or neither. That anatomical sorting is **odontogenic cyst classification by tooth relation**. Radicular cysts stay attached to a nonvital tooth apex and usually vanish after root canal therapy.
steps.say: Crown attached means dentigerous, apex attached means radicular, neither with keratin means keratocyst worry.

steps.tx: BRAF V600E mutation in many ameloblastomas opens targeted therapy conversations for unresectable or recurrent disease, while marsupialisation shrinks large lesions before definitive jaw surgery in selected patients. Molecular options extend **ameloblastoma management beyond resection alone**. Decompression over months can shrink a huge cystic tumour enough to preserve the inferior alveolar nerve.
steps.say: BRAF testing now matters in ameloblastoma; targeted drugs serve the unresectable few beside surgery.

steps.tx: Jaw radiolucency differential disciplines every case: ameloblastoma, keratocyst, dentigerous cyst, central giant cell granuloma, myxoma, and malignancy separated by locularity, tooth relation, and cortical behaviour. That differential is **radiolucent jaw lesion triage**. Cortical perforation with a soft tissue mass pushes any radiolucency toward tumour rather than simple cyst.
steps.say: Locularity, tooth relation, and cortical behaviour sort jaw radiolucencies before biopsy confirms.
